title: Disable unprivileged TTY line-discipline autoload

leads.summary: aarch64 packages discard the new sysctl setting
leads.consequence: The source-tree test passes, but both settings package recipes replace the entire sysctl drop-in with a two-line network-only file for aarch64. Fresh aarch64 installs never get dev.tty.ldisc_autoload=0; the new migration there reloads a file without the key and then gets marked done. Retain the new security key in each aarch64 replacement (or construct that replacement from only the excluded vm.* keys), and add an architecture-aware packaging check.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q1 a); coordinator also read PKGBUILD lines; published

leads.summary: Locally modified package-owned sysctl drop-ins can leave the hardening unapplied while the migration marks itself complete
leads.consequence: Both settings recipes declare 99-omarchy-sysctl.conf in backup=(). An existing admin-edited copy that pacman preserves in place when producing a .pacnew does not acquire the new key. The migration only checks readability, reapplies the old file, hides every failure, exits zero, and omarchy-migrate writes a permanent per-user success marker. Reboot still reads that unchanged old file. Detect absence of the new key on the *installed* file, give an actionable message about merging the .pacnew, and do not silently mark a failed security change applied.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q1 b, Q2); published

leads.summary: Another open PR already adds the same sysctl value, test pathname and migration body
leads.consequence: Open PR #12718 adds the identical config block, creates the same test pathname but with a hardcoded older migration path, and creates an otherwise identical migration as 1789261000.sh. Combining both branches needs resolution of the competing add/add test, and without removing one migration two per-user migrations run sudo sysctl -p on the entire same drop-in. If both migrations remain, #13311's grep | head test chooses the older timestamp, so deleting/breaking its own 1790423600.sh can still pass. Coordinate or deduplicate the migration and pin the surviving migration in the test.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q5, Q4); coordinator verified #12718 file list and author comment via gh; published

leads.summary: The 'btattach/ldattach/pppd are unaffected' comment omits the cold-load capability condition
leads.consequence: The kernel permits loading an *unregistered* ldisc when the caller has CAP_SYS_MODULE despite the disabled setting, not based on command name or UID alone. btattach and ldattach both issue TIOCSETD, so a user with tty access but without CAP_SYS_MODULE can get EPERM when the required module is not yet loaded. Loaded/built-in disciplines still work. Qualify the comment and document the cold-load tradeoff rather than promising these tools are categorically unaffected.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (Q3 nit); published as comment wording note

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Verified:** On x86_64 installs with an unmodified `/etc/sysctl.d/99-omarchy-sysctl.conf`, `dev.tty.ldisc_autoload=0` closes the unprivileged `TIOCSETD` module-autoload path. It applies at boot through systemd-sysctl, and after an update the migration applies it without a reboot. In `drivers/tty/tty_ldisc.c` (v7.1 to v7.3-rc4), `tty_ldisc_get()` returns `-EPERM` when the discipline is not registered, the caller lacks `CAP_SYS_MODULE` and the sysctl is 0. The Arch `linux` and `linux-omarchy` x86_64 configs ship `CONFIG_LDISC_AUTOLOAD=y` and `CONFIG_N_HDLC=m`, so the path is open by default today. Nothing in the Omarchy tree uses unprivileged line-discipline attach. The new test passes at head and fails on the base tree, and the full `test/shell` suite shows no new failures compared with base.

Three findings follow, starting with the overlap with #12718, then smaller notes on file mode, the test and the comment wording.

### The same change is still in open PR #12718

#12718 (same author, open) still carries a commit titled "Disable unprivileged TTY line-discipline autoload" with the same sysctl hunk and a byte-identical migration as `migrations/1789261000.sh`. It also adds `test/shell.d/sysctl-ldisc-autoload-test.sh`, which differs only in how it finds the migration. The author's note on #12718 says the ldisc part moved here, but the commit has not been dropped there.

**Impact:** If this PR lands first, #12718 hits an add/add conflict on the test file (checked with a local merge simulation onto current `quattro`). A resolution that keeps both files ships two migrations that run the same `sudo sysctl -p`. With both present, this PR's `grep -l ... | head -1` selector picks the older `1789261000.sh`, so the test would no longer check this PR's migration.

**Suggested change:** Drop the ldisc commit from #12718 so only one migration and one test ship.

### The key does not reach aarch64 or users who edited the drop-in

Both points are read from the `omacom/omarchy-pkgs` PKGBUILDs and pacman's documented backup behaviour. Neither was exercised with a real package install.

- On aarch64, `pkgbuilds/omarchy-settings/PKGBUILD` (and `omarchy-settings-dev`) overwrites `99-omarchy-sysctl.conf` with a heredoc that holds only `net.ipv4.tcp_mtu_probing=1`. The heredoc exists to drop the zram-specific `vm.*` tuning, but it also drops this non-memory key. The line is tty-core, not architecture-specific.
- The file is listed in `backup=()`. A user who edited it (for example to change `vm.swappiness`) keeps their copy, and the new line lands in a `.pacnew` that systemd-sysctl ignores. The migration then re-applies the old file and completes.

**Impact:** These two groups do not get the setting, neither at boot nor from the migration, and the migration reports nothing. Users with an edited file see only pacman's generic `.pacnew` warning, and get the setting only once they merge that file.

**Suggested change (optional approaches, a maintainer design choice):** Put the key in its own new drop-in, for example `etc/sysctl.d/90-omarchy-tty.conf`, and point the migration at that file. A new path installs even when the old file was edited, the aarch64 branch does not overwrite it, and the migration would no longer re-apply the other `vm.*` and network keys. Alternatively, keep the current file and add the line to the aarch64 heredoc in omarchy-pkgs if aarch64 should have it.

### The migration hides every failure and still records success

`sudo sysctl -p ... >/dev/null 2>&1 || true` discards all output and forces exit 0, so `omarchy-migrate` writes the completion marker regardless of outcome. Stubbed `sudo`/`sysctl` runs through a copy of `bin/omarchy-migrate`:

| case | exit | marker written | error shown | `reboot-required` set |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| sudo and sysctl succeed | 0 | yes | none | no |
| `sysctl` fails with an error | 0 | yes | none | no |
| `sudo` fails (wrong password) | 0 | yes | none | no |
| drop-in missing | 0 | yes | none | no |

**Impact:** The runtime value can stay at 1 until the next reboot with no indication. The effect is limited on x86_64 with an unmodified file, where boot applies the drop-in anyway.

**Suggested change:** Follow the repo's newer pattern in `migrations/1789294350.sh`: skip when the value is already set, keep stderr, and fall back to a reboot marker. Under the same stubs, this shape showed the error and set `reboot-required` when sudo or sysctl failed, and made no sudo call when the value was already 0:

```bash
echo "Disable unprivileged TTY line-discipline autoload"

if [[ $(sysctl -n dev.tty.ldisc_autoload) == "0" ]]; then
  exit 0
fi

sudo sysctl -p /etc/sysctl.d/99-omarchy-sysctl.conf >/dev/null || omarchy-state set reboot-required
```

`sysctl -p` ORs per-key results, so a failure in another key in the same file also sets `reboot-required`. A dedicated drop-in, as suggested above, avoids that.

**Migration file mode:** `migrations/1790423600.sh` is committed as 0755. `agents/skills/migrations.md` asks for 0644, as used by the other 128 migrations (and by the identical migration in #12718). It has no functional effect.

**Optional test improvement:** The migration checks only match strings, so the test still passes with the migration's `sudo sysctl -p` line commented out (the greps match the comment text) or with `sudo` removed. If no migration matches, it exits 1 without a `not ok` line, because the failing `grep -l ... | head -1` pipeline stops the script under `set -e` with `pipefail` before `fail` runs. `docs/testing.md` describes stubbing commands and running the migration as a convention for migration tests, as `test/shell.d/xps13-sidecar-amps-test.sh` does with the same `grep -l | head -1` form. Asserting the stubbed call log would catch both mutations. Otherwise, adding `|| true` to the selector restores the `not ok` message.

**Comment wording:** The drop-in comment says root, systemd and udev "still autoload normally, so btattach/ldattach/pppd are unaffected". The kernel gate is `CAP_SYS_MODULE`, not uid 0. Issue #9295 also names a real caveat that the comment omits: a daemon that drops privileges before attaching a discipline (gpsd with kernel PPS via `pps_ldisc`) now needs the module preloaded through `/etc/modules-load.d/`. One extra comment line would cover it.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Kernel, procps-ng 4.0.7 and omarchy-pkgs behaviour was read from source. The PR test (with mutants) and the full `test/shell` suite ran at base and head in an isolated sandbox; the same 10 environment-dependent test files fail in the sandbox at both base and head. The migration ran only with stubbed `sudo` and `sysctl`, so no real kernel value was changed or read. `.pacnew` handling, aarch64 package contents and the aarch64 kernel config were not tested. Overlap with #12718 and #12070 (which will conflict textually in the same file after either lands, a trivial rebase) was checked with a local merge simulation.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
